note: A proposal for review: how each current type would map to the service catalog. Within a type the first slice whose conditions all hold wins; the last slice of each type has none. Conditions: alert (the ticket parsed as an alert), source (how the classifier chose the type, such as rule:staff_logon), subject and text (case-insensitive regular expressions on the subject, or the subject and description).

discussions.title: Troubleshooting depth and timing
discussions.difference: Depth (investigating blocking against memory dump analysis or complex deadlock tracing) and timing (after a problem against before it).
discussions.why_hard: Most tickets start as general troubleshooting and only become advanced as the investigation goes on, so the opening text rarely shows the depth. Proactive work reads like a review request.
discussions.signals: Dump, deadlock graph or trace wording suggests Advanced; review, recommendation or tuning wording with no incident suggests Proactive.
options: Merge General and Advanced Troubleshooting. Their tier codes are identical, but General is coloured included and Advanced CE hours, so the colour question under Sheet rows to clarify decides whether merging changes coverage.
Default to General, and choose Advanced only on explicit dump or trace wording.
Let the DBA set the depth when closing the ticket.

discussions.title: Routine maintenance or index strategy
discussions.difference: Running the standard maintenance (index rebuilds, statistics, CHECKDB) against designing indexes (duplicates, missing indexes).
discussions.why_hard: Both mention indexes. The offering differs (CH in every tier against CE at Select and Signature), so a mistake changes billing.
discussions.signals: Job names such as IndexOptimize and statistics updates suggest maintenance; missing, duplicate or new index wording suggests strategy.
options: Keep both, separated by a keyword rule for job names.
Treat any index design request as Index Strategy & Optimization and everything run on a schedule as maintenance.

discussions.title: Best-practice settings or configuration changes
discussions.difference: Applying our baseline settings (MAXDOP, cost threshold, instant file initialization) against client-requested changes (memory limits, trace flags, instance settings).
discussions.why_hard: The same setting can be either; memory and instance settings appear under both descriptions. The difference is who asked and why, which the text often omits.
discussions.signals: SIP findings and named baseline settings suggest Best Practices; a client request for a specific change suggests Configuration Changes.
options: Keep a fixed list of baseline settings; everything else is a change.
Decide by who opened the ticket: our SIP or findings work against a client request.

discussions.title: Architecture and modernization
discussions.difference: Designing a deployment, designing a future topology, moving to PaaS, upgrading or migrating, and administering cloud databases.
discussions.why_hard: One project often covers several of these, and the current data has almost no design tickets to learn from.
discussions.signals: Upgrade or migration wording, and cloud platform names.
options: Merge the design categories (Planning & Design, Future State Architecture, Data Modernization); their tier codes and row colours are identical.
Keep them and let the DBA or the SOW name the category.

discussions.title: HA/DR monitoring, testing and development
discussions.difference: Watching availability group and cluster health against planned failover tests against building DR runbooks and AG setups.
discussions.why_hard: A failover can be a test, a fix or part of a build. Testing and development share an offering; monitoring does not.
discussions.signals: Alerts and health checks suggest monitoring; DR test and planned failover wording suggests testing; add, set up or build wording suggests development.
options: Merge HA/DR Management/Testing and HA/DR Development; their tier codes and row colours are identical.
Keep all three with keyword rules.

discussions.title: SIP, ad hoc and full assessments
discussions.difference: The recurring Strategic Improvement Plan against a one-off assessment the client requests against a full review of the data estate.
discussions.why_hard: All three are reviews. The scope and whether it was requested decide, and tickets named only "<Client> Assessment" carry neither.
discussions.signals: The SIP prefix marks plan work; scope wording (full, estate, architecture) suggests a Data Environment Assessment.
options: Use the SIP prefix for plan work and ask the team to name the assessment type in the subject.
Take the assessment type from the SOW or a ticket field.

discussions.title: Incident severity
discussions.difference: After-hours on-call support, Severity 1 total failures, unexpected crashes or storage loss, and corruption repair.
discussions.why_hard: These differ by severity and time of day more than by topic, and the ticket text rarely states the severity.
discussions.signals: The Zendesk priority, the time the ticket opened, and words such as P1, down or urgent.
options: Take severity from the Zendesk priority and opening time rather than from the text.
Merge Emergency Coverage and Critical Incidents if the team confirms they are the same.
